title: Amortize a host-bound decode step by validating multiple tokens per target pass

source.title: vLLM speculative decoding documentation
source.claim_scope: Speculative decoding is an architecture family for reducing inter-token latency; its benefit, acceptance rate and correctness remain model-, workload- and implementation-specific.

implementation_recipe: Profile a production-exact decode and separate target-model GPU work from the stable inter-token host or synchronization gap.
When per-step overhead is material, generate an architecture candidate that proposes multiple draft tokens and verifies them in one target step.
Prefer model-native draft heads when checkpoint support exists; otherwise compare external draft, n-gram and pipeline-overlap families under the same budget.
Prewarm the exact rejection-sampling and verification shapes before steady-state timing so runtime compilation is not counted as inference throughput.
validation_recipe: Freeze prompt tokens, sampling parameters, seed, dtype, CUDA-graph mode and output-length policy across baseline and candidate.
For temperature-zero inference, require exact output-token identity against the non-speculative greedy baseline before interpreting throughput.
At the first mismatch, compare target logits, decision margins and hidden states from the earliest multi-token verification before assuming recurrent-state rollback is responsible.
Measure acceptance length, rejected-token fraction, target passes, time to first token, inter-token latency and end-to-end throughput together.
Use a persistent engine and interleaved repetitions; report cold initialization, compilation and steady state separately.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Successful multi-token validation amortizes scheduler, input preparation, sampling and synchronization over accepted tokens.
Draft execution, rejection sampling and state rollback can replace the removed host gap as the next bottleneck.
Low acceptance can make the candidate slower even when its draft head is inexpensive.
failure_modes: Throughput is reported before verifying semantic equivalence to the frozen sampling contract.
Runtime JIT for rejection kernels contaminates the first measured samples.
A model-native draft head is assumed correct merely because the checkpoint contains weights.
The benchmark counts proposed tokens rather than accepted output tokens.
A batch-one latency win is generalized to throughput-oriented or multi-request workloads.
scope_limits: This is a candidate-generation prior, not a guarantee that speculative decoding is lossless or faster.

An RTX 4060 Qwen3.5-0.8B reproduction observed about 1.20-1.24x raw potential for native MTP-1, but failed exact greedy identity at output token four; the mismatch was localized to a BF16 near-tie with hidden-state differences already present in the first multi-token verification, before rollback could corrupt prior state.

An always-on FP32 lm_head restored 16-token agreement against an FP32 baseline for the reproduced prompt but made MTP slower than the stock BF16 baseline; that control is diagnostic evidence, not an accepted fix.
The technique changes model-level orchestration and may be outside a kernel-only task's public contract.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: One target-model pass and its host critical path produce one accepted output token.
algorithmic_decomposition.partition_axis: target verification step versus the variable number of accepted draft tokens
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: Accept the verified prefix, resample the first rejected position, and advance every model state only by the accepted-token count.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Emit only accepted tokens and preserve the baseline sampling distribution or exact greedy sequence required by the frozen contract.
algorithmic_decomposition.work_complexity: Adds draft work and verification while reducing the number of target steps per emitted token when acceptance exceeds one.
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: The serial decode span falls approximately with accepted tokens per target step, bounded by draft and verification dependencies.
algorithmic_decomposition.communication_cost: May add draft logits, token buffers and state-selection traffic, but amortizes host-device step coordination.
invariants: state advances by accepted tokens rather than proposed tokens
temperature-zero output matches the non-speculative greedy oracle under an exact contract
performance denominators count accepted output tokens
anti_patterns: optimize rejection kernels before measuring acceptance

candidate_archetypes.name: native draft-head target-step amortization
candidate_archetypes.template: Use the model's native draft head to propose a small token block, verify it in one target pass, and promote only widths that pass exactness and improve accepted-token latency.
